evidence.description: REQ-25's 'a div/mod-by-zero or parse error SHALL be caught' text is now traceable to concrete code, not just a comment claim: the header explicitly enumerates 5 malformed shapes (missing, N=0, negative, non-integer, leading-zero-octal) and each is independently falsifiable against the code below it -- re-derived all 5 by hand and confirmed each fails closed.

Re-derived FIND-001's fix by hand: raw='08' matches '^[0-9]+$' (digits='08'); n=$((10#08)) explicitly forces base-10 -> n=8 (never octal-parsed, since 10# overrides bash's default leading-zero-as-octal rule); n -eq 0 is false; prints '8'. raw='1-in-08' matches the 1-in-N regex, capturing digits='08', identical downstream normalization to n=8. raw='-3' still never reaches arithmetic at all (no regex matches a leading '-', return 1 at line 113) -- the fix does not touch or regress the pre-existing negative-N handling.

Read the full new test in isolation from its own PASS claim: 5 independently meaningful cases -- (1)/(2)/(3) ratio-string leading-zero shapes ('08','09','1-in-08') assert BOTH rc=0 AND absence of bash's literal octal-misparse error text AND correct DRAFT resolution; (4) a wake-counter FILE corrupted to '08' asserts the counter is normalized to 8 then incremented to 9 (verified against the actual post-run file content on disk, not just STATE.md), directly closing FIND-001's wake-counter half of the hazard; (5) is a POSITIVE 4-wake end-to-end cycle for '1-in-04' proving leading-zero ratios are correctly NORMALIZED (not merely rejected) to the exact same N-1-Mode-A/1-Mode-B pattern as a plain '1-in-4' (cross-checked against test-prop26c's own established oracle pattern), which is a materially stronger proof than a bare crash-absence check.

This is genuine RED-phase evidence, not a trusted self-claim: the log shows the NEW test-prop26d run against the git-HEAD (pre-fix) run.sh inside a scratch copy and it FAILS on exactly the predicted assertions ('no raw bash octal-misparse error text leaked' fails in 4 of 5 cases, plus the counter-normalization assertion), while all 33 pre-existing test files (including test-prop26a/b/c) remain green against that SAME pre-fix run.sh -- proving this is a genuinely new, previously-uncovered gap, not a regression in already-covered behavior.
Full 34/34 PASS against the post-fix run.sh, test-prop26d included, zero regression in the other 33 files (test-prop26a/b/c's original 4-case/mutation/1-in-N oracles unaffected).

Traced FIND-002's 'inconsistent guard between two arithmetic sites' by hand across the CURRENT code and found the guard now applied at THREE distinct arithmetic sites with an identical pattern (`if ! X=$((10#$Y)) 2>/dev/null; then <fail-closed>; fi`): (1) line 119 inside _modeb_ratio_n before the -eq-0 check, (2) line 144 inside _modeb_next_wake_count before the increment, (3) lines 166-167 immediately before the actual `wake_n_safe % ratio_n_safe` modulo that decides effective_mode=B -- this is the exact site FIND-002 named as previously unguarded (old line ~133). The decision-making modulo site is no longer relying on incidental bash short-circuit behavior; it has its own explicit, deliberate, fail-closed guard.

Verified the belt-and-suspenders re-normalization at lines 166-167 cannot introduce a NEW defect: both $wake_n (from _modeb_next_wake_count's `printf '%s' "$nxt"` where nxt=$((cur+1)), always a clean bash-arithmetic-produced decimal string) and $ratio_n (from _modeb_ratio_n's `printf '%s' "$n"` where n=$((10#$digits)), likewise always clean decimal) are guaranteed to already be leading-zero-free by construction before they ever reach lines 166-167 -- so this second guard is provably a no-op safety net, never a spurious fail-closed on a value that should have resolved to Mode B.

Independently enumerated every arithmetic expansion in run.sh (lines 119, 122, 144, 147, 166, 167, and the unrelated round-counter arithmetic at 319/322/344). Confirmed the round-counter sites are fed only by an internal loop variable that starts at 1 and is incremented by the script itself (never by an externally-supplied/corruptible ratio or counter-file string), so they are outside FIND-001/002's threat class and require no guard. No unguarded ratio/wake-counter arithmetic site remains anywhere in the file.

The fix is a single, consistently-documented normalization idiom (`$((10#$x))`) applied identically at all three call sites, with each site's comment explicitly cross-referencing FIND-001/FIND-002 and explaining WHY (not a copy-pasted mystery guard) -- no duplication of divergent logic, no dead code introduced, and the pre-existing regex-based rejection of negative/non-integer/missing values (lines 104-114) is left untouched and unduplicated by the new base-10 guard, which only handles the leading-zero/overflow sub-case the regexes cannot.

Genuine, independently-checkable RED->GREEN evidence trail specific to THIS fix round exists (distinct from the original 9-target-feature sprint-4-red/green-phase.log pair): RED shows the new discriminating test failing against the unmodified pre-fix run.sh with the exact predicted symptom, GREEN shows all 34 files (33 baseline + the 1 new file) passing against the fixed run.sh -- this is not a fake-to-pass log; the failure text in the RED log names the specific assertions that failed, consistent with the octal-misparse hazard's known symptom.
